summary.headline: PDS posts record Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹4,432 crores (+30% YoY), EBITDA up 49% to ₹153 crores, and turns net cash of ₹154 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the highest quarterly revenue in PDS history, with revenue up 29% QoQ and 30% YoY, and H1 revenue up 23% to ₹7,876 crores. EBITDA margin rose to 3.5% (up 44 bps YoY, 66 bps QoQ) and PAT reached ₹70 crores, with the Americas growing 54% in Q2. Working capital turned negative (-5 days) and net debt of ₹105 crores at March became net cash of ₹154 crores at September. Management kept a cautious tone on FY27 growth guidance, citing a 13% order book increase, and flagged Ted Baker/New Lobster as a priority problem.

Higher asset base after Knit Gallery acquisition and UK office

financial_highlights.metric: Sourcing segment revenue and EBIT (H1 FY27)
Investment in new verticals (H1 FY27, through P&L)

segments.name: Sourcing
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue ₹7,542 crores (+25% YoY) with EBIT of ₹175 crores at a 2.3% margin. Americas revenue grew 54% in Q2 and 44% in H1, with the U.S. about 23% of business.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue ₹452 crores, almost flat YoY, with EBIT of ₹26 crores at a 5.8% margin. Management said Q2 manufacturing margin fell to about 2.8%, with Bangladesh flat and Knit Gallery growing.

segments.name: Ted Baker / New Lobster
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 income from operations about ₹268 crores (~30% up from ₹205 crores); loss about ₹11 crores vs ₹30 crores in H1 FY26. Gross margin about 22% in H1 (30% in Q1, 22% in Q2) vs 18% last year.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue guidance; management said it will remain cautious and expects to sustain a mid-teens growth trajectory over time.
Management targets EBITDA margin expansion of 50-70 bps and PAT margin expansion of 50-75 bps every year, with PAT margin nearing 3% in 2-3 years.
Employee cost growth expected at 5-7% for FY27, with an effort to hold it at or below FY26 levels.
Finance costs guided not to rise vs last year and to fall in Q3 and Q4 as long-term debt is prepaid.
New-vertical P&L investment: annualised run-rate around ₹70 crores vs a ₹80 crores FY27 target; maintainable level ₹40-50 crores.
Minority interest expected to ease toward about 25% of PAT within 2-3 quarters as New Lobster losses and manufacturing improve.
U.S. could be 40-50% of business in 4-5 years, per Pallak Seth.
Ted Baker/New Lobster: options under review with ABG, including breakeven measures, partnerships, or sale/restructuring within FY27.
capex_capacity: Investment in new verticals H1 FY27 ₹34 crores vs target of ~₹80 crores for FY27 (from ₹168 crores in FY25).
Knit Gallery (India factory) growing; management aims to lift average selling price in kids category from $1.00-1.20 to $1.50.
Partnership with Busana Group of Indonesia (July 2026) for Bangladesh factory, aimed at higher-value orders and worker skill upgrades.
Technology programme across six areas including SAP S/4HANA, procurement, real-time factory quality, AI-led design and pricing, and master data management.
Prepaid one ₹35 crore long-term facility from Bajaj Finance at India standalone level in Q2; evaluating further prepayments.
DBS Lifestyle divested; Design Arc earlier merged into Poeticgem.
demand_pricing: Order book ₹5,670 crores as of October 2026, up ~13% YoY; management said the sequential order book dipped on seasonality.
French retailer Sourcing as a Service contract: 5-year, multiyear (3-4 years typical), about $550 million annual managed volume and roughly $200 million in year 1 per management.
U.S. contract of about $50 million revenue; year 1 estimated at about $10 million (~₹100 crores). Neither new contract contributed meaningfully to H1 GMV.
H1 GMV ₹11,366 crores vs ₹10,100 crores last year (+12.5%).
U.S. H1 sales about $184 million; Kohl's about $31 million, Fashion Nova about $40 million (+54%), Walmart about $20 million.
Of the top 10 U.S. retailers, 7 have opened accounts with PDS. Zamira U.S. sales rose from $11.5 million to $21.4 million; Krayons grew 21%; PDS Asia Star (China) grew 47%.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth guidance applies for FY27 and how should FY28 look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numeric guidance, citing a tough geopolitical and inflation backdrop. It pointed to H1 revenue +23% and order book +13% as nine-month visibility, and aims to stay close to mid-teens growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin hold at about 3.5% despite the rise in employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q2 employee cost jump was largely incentive payouts and increments preponed from October to July, which should normalise in Q3. It also set a target of 50-70 bps EBITDA margin expansion a year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expense levers and steady-state employee cost growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth of about 5-7% a year is the norm, with FY27 held at or below FY26 levels. Other expenses include semi-variable freight, licence and royalty fees, and legal costs, and are expected to decline as operating leverage builds.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new-vertical investment and will it stay at breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 new-vertical investment was ₹34 crores, annualising to about ₹70 crores. Management said the maintainable level is ₹40-50 crores and that there is headroom to reduce further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Ted Baker/New Lobster and its gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is exploring options with ABG, including a breakeven plan, a third-party tie-up, or further relocation and cost cuts. Gross margin was about 22% in H1, down from 30% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the drop in manufacturing profitability and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a change of management 2-3 quarters ago, customer caution on Bangladesh orders, and flat Bangladesh revenue. Recovery levers are Knit Gallery growth, price-point moves to $1.50 and the Busana partnership.

risks_watch: Ted Baker/New Lobster: H1 income from operations ~₹268 crores but still loss-making (~₹11 crores); management says it is not happy and will act within FY27 (ABG options, breakeven plan, possible sale/restructuring, further relocation).
Order book growth: ~13% YoY at ₹5,670 crores but sequentially dipped on seasonality; management said Q4 and Q1 order book is hard to predict.

Manufacturing: Q2 margin fell to ~2.8% after management change; Bangladesh revenue flat with customer caution on Bangladesh allocations; recovery depends on Knit Gallery growth, $1.50 ASP move and Busana partnership.
Minority interest rising (management cited ~39% of PAT in the quarter); management expects a fall toward ~25% within 2-3 quarters as New Lobster losses and manufacturing improve.
Employee and other expense trajectory: Q2 jump partly preponed incentives/increments; management expects normalisation in Q3 but has not quantified steady-state other expenses.
Margin targets: management is holding to 50-70 bps EBITDA margin expansion a year and has moved away from the earlier 555 aspiration, citing caution on balance sheet and ROCE.
key_quotes: The quarter 2 of FY27 marks a significant milestone for PDS with the highest quarterly revenue in our history.
But I think in our own assessment, we are not happy with the performance as of now.
So this is one of the high priorities of the management at this stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, growth in the Americas and the balance sheet, but deliberately cautious on FY27 and FY28 numbers, declining to give numeric revenue guidance and citing geopolitics, inflation and high interest rates. Management was notably frank that Ted Baker/New Lobster is not meeting its expectations and is a top priority, while being defensive and vague on the timing of margin expansion.

adds.what: Knit Gallery India factory growth (no new capacity count stated)

growth.why: No formal FY27 revenue guidance; management stays cautious but aspires to a maintainable mid-teens growth trajectory, backed by a order book of ₹5,670 crores (~+13% YoY as of October) and a French Sourcing-as-a-Service contract (~$200m year-1 managed volume), with Q2 revenue +30% YoY and EBITDA +49%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 50-70 bps annual EBITDA margin expansion (Q2 EBITDA margin 3.5%, +44 bps YoY), and new-vertical spend is falling (H1 ₹34 crores vs ₹72 crores, -53%), though Q2 employee cost was inflated by preponed incentives and timing of expansion is vague.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or store capacity was announced; the only capacity item is Knit Gallery factory growth with no capacity count, and capex is not discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 GMV grew 12.5% (₹11,366 crores vs ₹10,100 crores), order book is ~13% up YoY at ₹5,670 crores, and management aims for a mid-teens growth trajectory, though it gave no numeric FY27 guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond a ₹35 crore debt prepayment and the technology programme, and no utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined numeric revenue guidance and stayed cautious citing geopolitics, inflation and high rates, despite H1 revenue +23% and Q2 +30% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ted Baker/New Lobster is still loss-making (~₹11 crores in H1) and manufacturing margin fell to ~2.8% in Q2, while the order book dipped sequentially on seasonality and Q4-Q1 visibility is weak.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or brand launch was discussed; the Busana partnership and $1.50 price-point move are upgrades to existing lines, not launches.

rows.label: Ted Baker/New Lobster breakeven or exit
rows.why: H1 income from operations is about ₹268 crores with a loss of ~₹11 crores (vs ₹30 crores last year), and management is reviewing ABG options including breakeven, partnership or sale within FY27.

rows.label: Net cash and lower finance costs
rows.why: Net debt of ₹105 crores in March became net cash of ₹154 crores in September, and finance costs are guided to fall in Q3 and Q4 as long-term debt is prepaid.

rows.label: US and French Sourcing-as-a-Service ramp
rows.why: Americas grew 54% in Q2, the French contract carries ~$200 million year-1 managed volume, and the US contract adds ~$10 million (~₹100 crores) in year 1, though neither contributed meaningfully to H1.

tone.note: Management was confident on Americas growth, the balance sheet and execution but cautious on FY27/FY28 numbers, declining numeric guidance; analysts pressed on Ted Baker/New Lobster, manufacturing margins and expense normalisation.
